## Why This Is Asked
Tests basic CKAD patterns: per-namespace CronJob, PVC-backed data, secret-backed credentials, config-driven parameters, and a namespace-scoped NetworkPolicy. It also touches operational concerns like retention and boundary scoping.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob and Job workflows for scheduled data tasks
- PVC data access and tar-based backups
- Secrets and ConfigMaps for credentials and config
- InitContainers for tooling setup
- Namespace NetworkPolicy for egress control

## Code Example
```yaml
# CronJob skeleton
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: ns-backup
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: backup-sa
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          volumes:
          - name: data
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: ns-data-pvc
          - name: backup
            emptyDir: {}
          initContainers:
          - name: install-tools
            image: alpine:3.18
            command: ["sh","-c","apk add --no-cache aws-cli tar gzip"]
          containers:
          - name: backup
            image: amazon/aws-cli:2
            command: ["sh","-c","tar czf /backup/namespace.tar.gz -C /data . && aws s3 cp /backup/namespace.tar.gz s3://$(BUCKET)/namespace-$(date +%F).tar.gz"]
            envFrom:
            - secretRef:
                name: backup-creds
            - configMapRef:
                name: backup-config
            volumeMounts:
            - name: data
              mountPath: /data
            - name: backup
              mountPath: /backup
```

## Code Example

apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: image-processor
  namespace: batch
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      parallelism: 25
      completions: 500
      ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 3600
      backoffLimit: 3
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
            - name: seed-work
              image: busybox
              command: ["sh", "-c", "cp /config/files /work/"]

## Why This Is Asked

This question tests practical CKAD skills: dynamic configuration via ConfigMaps, per-namespace isolation, InitContainers, health checks, logging, and network policy considerations.

## Key Concepts

- **Namespace-scoped ConfigMaps**: Enable dynamic feature flags without pod restarts
- **InitContainers**: Provide bootstrap tooling (curl) before the main container starts
- **Conditional sidecars**: Driven by ConfigMap values to enable canary deployments
- **Readiness and liveness probes**: Ensure controller and application health
- **PVC-backed logs**: Provide persistent storage for debugging and audit trails
- **NetworkPolicies**: Enforce zero-trust networking by restricting egress to known endpoints

## Trade-offs

| Aspect | Consideration |
|--------|----------------|
| **Polling Interval** | Frequent polls increase API load; infrequent polls delay flag propagation |
| **ConfigMap Updates** | Applications must watch or periodically read the ConfigMap to detect changes |
| **Sidecar Overhead** | Running a sidecar even when disabled consumes resources; consider whether the main container can react to flag changes directly |
| **Egress Restriction** | Locking down NetworkPolicy requires knowing all upstream dependencies upfront |
| **Log Persistence** | PVCs add operational complexity and cost; consider external logging solutions for production |

metadata:
  name: feature-flags

---

kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: flag-poller
  namespace: feature-flags
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: flag-poller

    metadata:

        app: flag-poller
    spec:

        - name: install-curl
          image: curlimages/curl:latest

          volumeMounts:
            - name: tools
              mountPath: /tools
      containers:

          image: your-poller-image:latest
          command: ['/bin/sh', '-c', 'while true; do curl -s $FLAGS_API > /config/flags.json; sleep 60; done']
          volumeMounts:
            - name: config
              mountPath: /config
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10

            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 8080

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests your ability to design an isolated audit pattern with in-cluster API access, RBAC scoping, and security boundaries.

## Key Concepts
- Namespace-scoped RBAC for fine-grained access control
- In-cluster API access using Secrets and ConfigMaps
- PVC-backed persistent logs and InitContainers for tooling
- NetworkPolicy for egress control to restrict traffic to the collector
- Health checks (readiness/liveness probes) for reliability

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: audit-baseline
  namespace: example
data:
  baseline.json: |
    {"pods": [], "services": []}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: audit-auth
  namespace: example
type: Opaque
stringData:
  token: " collector-auth-token"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: audit-logs
  namespace: example
spec:
  accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: audit-agent
  namespace: example
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: audit-agent
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: audit-agent
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: installer
        image: busybox
        command: ["sh", "-c", "apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl jq && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tools
          mountPath: /tools
      containers:
      - name: auditor
        image: your-audit-image:latest
        command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "while true; do audit.sh; sleep 60; done"]
        env:
        - name: COLLECTOR_URL
          value: "http://collector.audit-system.svc.cluster.local:8080"
        - name: AUTH_TOKEN
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: audit-auth
              key: token
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
        - name: tools
          mountPath: /tools
        - name: baseline
          mountPath: /baseline
          readOnly: true
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /ready
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20
      volumes:
      - name: logs
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: audit-logs
      - name: tools
        emptyDir: {}
      - name: baseline
        configMap:
          name: audit-baseline
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: audit-egress-restrict
  namespace: example
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: audit-agent
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: audit-system
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: collector
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8080
```

## Trade-offs
- **Pros**: Namespace isolation ensures audit agents don't interfere; NetworkPolicy provides security; PVC enables log persistence for compliance
- **Cons**: Each namespace requires separate Deployment (use Operator/Controller to automate); InitContainer adds startup latency; per-namespace RBAC management overhead increases with cluster size
